name: only ClassCastException mentioned vs mentions any other exception
side_a: No deduction: the answer mentions only ClassCastException (the correct exception) and does not bring up any other exception type.
side_b: Deduct 2 points: the answer mentions any additional exception type (e.g., NullPointerException) even if hedged or described as a later possibility.

name: acknowledges possible ClassCastException vs denies it can happen
side_a: Credit the answer when it explicitly states that a ClassCastException **can** be thrown at the cast site (e.g., “can occur”, “will be thrown”, “is unsafe”).
side_b: Deduct when the answer asserts or strongly implies that a ClassCastException **cannot** occur at that line (e.g., “won’t throw”, “cannot happen”, “the cast is safe”), even if it gives other correct information.

name: mentions possible NullPointerException vs does not mention NullPointerException
side_a: Credit answers that explicitly note that a NullPointerException could occur (e.g., when the fragment is null).
side_b: Deduct answers that never mention a NullPointerException, even if they discuss null handling.

name: explicit‑null‑check discussion vs none
side_a: Answers that explicitly explain how the null‑check (or casting null) affects the possibility of a ClassCastException are credited.
side_b: Answers that do not mention the null‑check or its safety are deducted.

name: explicit‑null‑cast‑safe claim vs no such claim
side_a: Do NOT claim that the cast is safe when the fragment is null (i.e., no statement that ‘casting null yields null’).
side_b: Explicitly state that casting a null fragment is safe (e.g., ‘casting null yields null’).

name: mentions NullPointerException vs mentions only ClassCastException
side_a: Discuss only the possible ClassCastException from the unsafe cast.
side_b: Also mention a possible NullPointerException (or other exception) besides ClassCastException.
